sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Vasubandhu** ​(*vasubandhu*) — ‌Abhidharma, Yogacara ‌· ​The celebrated ​Buddhist ​scholar — ​author of ​the ‌Abhidharmakośa, co-founder ​of ​the Yogācāra ‌school — ​belongs ‌to the ​Buddhist ‌tradition, where ​it is ​catalogued ​under the ​domain ​"Abhidharma, Yogacara". ‌The name ​means ‌"The celebrated ​Buddhist ‌scholar — ​author of ‌the ​Abhidharmakośa, co-founder ‌of ​the Yogācāra ​school".

**Vasubandhu** ‌is ‌abhidharma, yogacara. ‌The ​name means ​"The celebrated ‌Buddhist ​scholar — ​author ‌of the ​Abhidharmakośa, co-founder ​of ‌the Yogācāra ​school" ‌and belongs ​to the ​buddhist ​tradition.

PuniCodex ​restores ‌the name ‌as **Vasubandhu** ​and ‌serves its ​temple ​at [its ‌temple](https://punicodex.com/vasubandhu/). The ‌restoration ‌needs no ‌distinctive ​letters or ‌diacritics its ​ASCII ​form would ​lose, ‌which places ​the name ​in ​Tier 2. ‌The ​plain ASCII ​form *vasubandhu* ​survives ‌as a ​modern ‌convenience imposed ​by the ‌early ​domain-name system; ‌the ‌restoration, not ​the fallback, ​is ​the form ​the ‌project defends ‌as philologically ​complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Devanagari as ​**वसुबन्धु**. ​Etymologically it ​means "The ​celebrated ​Buddhist scholar ‌— author ​of the ​Abhidharmakośa, ‌co-founder of ​the Yogācāra ‌school".

​The ASCII ‌form *vasubandhu* ​survives only ​because ​the early ​domain-name system ​could ‌not carry ​diacritics; it ‌is a ​technological ‌compromise, not ​an ancient ‌spelling. ​The Unicode ‌restoration **Vasubandhu** ​recovers the ​full ‌diacritic detail ‌of the ‌scholarly ​transliteration directly ​in the ‌address bar. ​The ​restoration needs ‌no distinctive ​letters ​or diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form would ‌lose, ​which places ​the name ​in ​Tier 2.

‌The letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

​- ‌**v** → ​**V** — ​Same, ‌capitalized
- ‌**a** → ‌**a** — ‌Same
​- **s** ‌→ **s** ​— ​Same
- ​**u** → ‌**u** — ​Same
​- **b** ​→ **b** ‌— ​Same
- ​**a** → ​**a** — ‌Same
​- **n** ‌→ **n** ​— ‌Same
- ​**d** → ‌**d** — ‌Same
​- **h** ​→ **h** ​— ​Same
- ‌**u** → ‌**u** — ​Same

sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/vasubandhu/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**vasubandhu** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Vasubandhu.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"vasubandhu" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Vasubandhu".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"vasubandhu" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Vasubandhu" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Vasubandhu was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Vasubandhu ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Vasubandhu ‌place abhidharma, ​yogacara ​at the ​center ​of a ​living ‌mythological world.

​### ​Origins (Myth)

‌Vasubandhu ​appears in ‌buddhist ​tradition as ‌abhidharma, ​yogacara. The ​name's ​meaning, "The ​celebrated ​Buddhist scholar ‌— ​author of ‌the ​Abhidharmakośa, co-founder ‌of ​the Yogācāra ‌school", ​shapes the ‌narratives ​told about ​this ‌figure.

### ‌Worship ‌and Memory ​(Cult)

​Devotees and ‌later ​tradition-keepers preserved ​Vasubandhu ‌in ritual, ​text, ​and iconography, ‌ensuring ​the name ‌survived ​into the ​modern ​scholarly record.

​The ‌myths of ‌Vasubandhu ​survive in ‌fragments, ​summaries, and ​later ‌retellings. Each ‌version ‌reflects the ‌interests ​of its ‌tellers ​— poets, ​priests, ​philosophers, and ‌scholars. ​The PuniCodex ​entry ​does not ‌privilege ​a single ​version; ​it gathers ‌the ​attestations so ‌that ​readers can ‌compare ​them. The ‌restoration ‌Vasubandhu gives ​the ​figure a ​stable ​name around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.label: Archaeology & Material Evidence
sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Vasubandhu ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Buddhist ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌वसुबन्धु, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​abhidharma ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To ​contemplate Vasubandhu ‌is ‌to hold ​the ​idea of ​abhidharma, ​Yogacara ​in the ‌mind ​and to ​ask ‌what of ​it ‌endures. The ​name ‌means "The ​celebrated ​Buddhist scholar ​— ​author of ​the ‌Abhidharmakośa, ​co-founder of ‌the ​Yogācāra school" ‌— ​and a ‌name ​that carries ‌its ​meaning so ​openly ‌invites meditation ‌rather ‌than mere ​recollection. ​The ‌tradition remembers ​the ​name as ‌abhidharma, ​Yogacara · ​The ‌celebrated Buddhist ​scholar ‌— author ​of ​the Abhidharmakośa, ​co-founder ​of the ‌Yogācāra ‌school.

​Sit with ‌the ​restored form ​— ‌Vasubandhu — ‌and ‌the diacritics ‌themselves ​become the ‌practice: ​each mark ​is ​a small ‌act ​of ​attention, a ​refusal ‌to let ​the ​plain ASCII ​form ‌*vasubandhu* stand ​in ‌for the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved in ‌this ​name, ​the restoration ​asks ​the reader ‌to ‌preserve in ​turn.
